title: The model, validated and read
intro: plan reads a canonical project model and moves one issue through it. Status is never stored — it is derived from what was recorded about an issue and from the state of its dependencies. Every scenario here is executed against the real binary by test/cases/34_command_fixtures.sh.

scenarios.title: A model that parses and hangs together
scenarios.explain: Schemas, references, the dependency graph and status consistency, in one pass. A key nobody reads is an error here for the same reason it is an error in the policy: an unread field is a belief nothing checks.

scenarios.title: A repository with no project model
scenarios.explain: Exit 12 is MISSING_ARTIFACT: the repository is not set up for a project model, which is a different fact from a model that fails to parse.

scenarios.title: What can be started now
scenarios.explain: I0002 depends on I0001, so only I0001 is ready. Readiness is derived from the graph rather than labelled on the issue, so it cannot disagree with the dependencies.

scenarios.title: What is waiting, and on what
scenarios.explain: The complement of ready, and it names the dependency rather than only the fact of being blocked — the useful question is what to finish first.

scenarios.title: A subcommand it does not have
scenarios.explain: Exit 2 is USAGE. A mistyped subcommand is refused rather than treated as a default, so a script cannot silently ask a different question from the one it meant.
